name: Dimethyl fumarate
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Disease-specific models directly link p.N237S ACOX1 to excess oxidants, 4-HNE, and glial injury and show rescue by peroxisomal catalase, though human cell-resolved redox pathology is absent. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: A preconditioning schedule that raises NRF2-linked glutathione capacity is a coherent compensatory bridge, but early thiol depletion and uncertain parent-versus-metabolite activity are material directional assumptions. Sources: DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0120254; DOI:10.1155/2017/6093903
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: DMF directly modifies KEAP1 cysteines, drives NRF2 nuclear signaling, and induces glutathione-redox adaptations, with a well-defined but schedule-dependent initial glutathione cost. Sources: DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0120254; DOI:10.1155/2017/6093903
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Human dosing induces NRF2-dependent genes and yields measurable CSF monomethyl fumarate, making CNS reach plausible, but intact parent DMF is not quantifiable in plasma and relevant glial exposure remains uncertain. Sources: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/product-information/tecfidera-epar-product-information_en.pdf; DOI:10.1016/j.msard.2021.102861
empirical_translation_rationale: Low-micromolar DMF preconditioning protected a human oligodendrocyte line from peroxide challenge and exact-drug studies show beneficial CNS-cell and microglial phenotypes, albeit outside ACOX1 disease. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.redox.2015.04.011; DOI:10.1124/jpet.111.190132; DOI:10.1186/s12974-018-1125-5
hypothesis_report: Dimethyl fumarate is a testable, schedule-dependent compensatory hypothesis for Mitchell syndrome rather than an inhibitor of the causal ACOX1 gain of function: p.N237S stabilizes the active ACOX1 dimer, increases hydrogen peroxide and 4-HNE-marked oxidative damage in variant-expression models, and is associated with wrapping-glial and Schwann-cell death, while peroxisomal catalase rescues major fly phenotypes, together supporting the directional inference that raising glial peroxide tolerance could reduce injury even if ACOX1 flux remains abnormal [DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021]. DMF covalently modifies KEAP1 cysteines, drives NRF2 nuclear accumulation, and produces a strong transcriptional response, but it also acutely consumes glutathione before levels recover above baseline [DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0120254]; separate experiments support induction of glutathione reductase and glutathione recycling [DOI:10.1155/2017/6093903] and increased glutathione, redox potential, and oxidant-challenge survival in CNS cells [DOI:10.1124/jpet.111.190132]. In a human oligodendrocyte line, 1-10 micromolar DMF preconditioning protected against a 400-micromolar hydrogen-peroxide challenge after 72 hours but not after 24 hours, making time-dependent adaptation rather than immediate antioxidant activity the relevant proposed action [DOI:10.1016/j.redox.2015.04.011]; suppression of LPS-activated microglial inflammatory signaling and microglia-mediated neuronal toxicity offers a second possible lesion-amplification route, although that result used an exogenous stimulus and does not establish that accumulated Mitchell-syndrome microglia are pathogenic [DOI:10.1186/s12974-018-1125-5]. Translation is materially uncertain: the human white-matter redox bridge is inferred from overexpression, peripheral-glial, and invertebrate systems, wild-type ACOX1 overexpression was itself toxic, terminal human tissue cannot order axonal, myelin, glial, and myeloid injury, and a zebrafish model showed neither oligodendrocyte loss nor induction of several assayed antioxidant transcripts while revealing peroxisome loss and integrated-stress-response activation as rival or parallel processes [DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894; DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886]. Exposure also qualifies the mechanism: oral DMF is rapidly hydrolysed to active monomethyl fumarate and intact DMF is not quantifiable in plasma, so direct CNS or peripheral-glial KEAP1 alkylation by the parent compound cannot be assumed even though Nrf2-dependent genes are induced in treated humans [https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/product-information/tecfidera-epar-product-information_en.pdf]; in a 16-person secondary-progressive-MS study, CSF monomethyl fumarate reached 11% of plasma and three participants stopped by week 6 because of persistent adverse effects [DOI:10.1016/j.msard.2021.102861], whereas a 54-person placebo-controlled primary-progressive-MS trial found no effect on CSF neurofilament light or other efficacy outcomes over 48 weeks and observed more infections, lymphopenia, flushing, and gastrointestinal events [DOI:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001037]. The exact compound nevertheless satisfies established human-use qualification because Tecfidera contains dimethyl fumarate and has renewed EU marketing authorisation for relapsing-remitting MS from age 13, with lymphopenia, opportunistic infection/PML, gastrointestinal effects, and liver injury constraining chronic experimental exposure [https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/product-information/tecfidera-epar-product-information_en.pdf]; no published Mitchell-syndrome or endogenous ACOX1-p.N237S use or test was identified. A discriminating experiment should therefore compare clinically bounded DMF and monomethyl-fumarate exposures, preconditioning and post-injury schedules, in endogenous heterozygous patient-derived CNS glia and sensory-neuron-Schwann-cell co-cultures, measuring parent/metabolite exposure, nuclear NRF2 and target induction, time-resolved GSH/GSSG, peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide, 4-HNE, microglial secretome, and cell/axon survival; target engagement without a net fall in oxidant damage or improved survival, or early thiol depletion with worsened injury, would refute the proposed rescue window.

name: Ebselen
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: p.N237S models directly establish excess ACOX1 activity, peroxide, 4-HNE, and glial injury with major phenotypic rescue by peroxisomal catalase, albeit without human tissue redox confirmation. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Catalytic peroxide and hydroperoxide reduction offers a coherent downstream rescue route, but relevant thiol availability and peroxisomal-interface access are unproven and broad selenium-thiol actions can oppose benefit. Sources: PMID:2107391; DOI:10.1073/pnas.122061399
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Multiple exact-compound studies establish glutathione-peroxidase-like catalytic reduction of hydrogen peroxide and organic hydroperoxides, tempered by broad thiol oxidation and mitochondrial effects. Sources: DOI:10.1016/0006-2952(88)90591-6; PMID:2107391; DOI:10.1179/135100000101535924
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Completed human auditory dosing and functional observations make tissue reach plausible, but no study establishes cochlear, CNS, or peroxisomal target-site concentration or biochemical engagement. Sources: DOI:10.1016/s0140-6736(17)31791-9; NCT04677972
empirical_translation_rationale: Exact-drug neuronal peroxide protection and a placebo-controlled human noise challenge provide adjacent drug-specific phenotypes, but the human auditory response was non-monotonic and not mechanism-specific. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2004.04.055; DOI:10.1016/s0140-6736(17)31791-9
hypothesis_report: Ebselen is a biologically coherent but compartment-dependent redox-buffering hypothesis for ACOX1 p.N237S Mitchell syndrome: it catalyses thiol-supported reduction of hydrogen peroxide and organic hydroperoxides with glutathione-peroxidase-like kinetics (DOI:10.1016/0006-2952(88)90591-6; PMID:2107391), whereas the variant forms an abundant, turnover-resistant active dimer, has about 40% greater activity per unit protein, raises hydrogen peroxide, ROS and 4-HNE in fly and primary-Schwann-cell overexpression systems, and its major fly phenotypes were rescued by added peroxisomal catalase (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021). The directional inference is that, without correcting ACOX1 abundance or dimerisation, sufficient ebselen and reducing thiol at the peroxisomal-cytosolic redox interface could lower peroxide and lipid-hydroperoxide propagation and secondarily preserve vulnerable glia, axons, auditory function and optic-pathway tissue; protection of mouse neuronal cells from exogenous hydrogen peroxide supports the proposed action but is not disease-model evidence (DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2004.04.055). Human auditory translation is suggestive but non-specific: in an 83-participant healthy-adult noise-challenge trial, oral ebselen reduced the 4-kHz temporary threshold shift by 68% at 400 mg twice daily and was reported well tolerated, but the 200- and 600-mg arms were null, giving a non-monotonic response (PMID:28716314); posted results from a mechanistically different Phase 3 Meniere study with 28-day treatment and 84-day outcomes show more low-frequency-threshold and Words-in-Noise responders on ebselen than placebo, but no inferential effect analysis is posted, treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 59/112 versus 45/108 participants, serious events in 2/112 versus 0/108, and the open-label extension documents exposure up to 360 days (NCT04677972). These studies establish completed Phase-I-equivalent human dosing but not exposure in cochlear, optic-pathway, CNS or peroxisomal compartments, nor chronic tolerability in children; current approval or marketed use was not established and NCATS lists ebselen as investigational (https://drugs.ncats.io/substance/40X2P7DPGH), while no exact Mitchell-syndrome or ACOX1 p.N237S use or testing was identified. Important counterweights are that the disease evidence relies substantially on overexpression systems in which wild-type ACOX1 was itself toxic, human neural tissue has not demonstrated peroxide or 4-HNE excess, the zebrafish model did not reproduce several oxidative or inflammatory transcript changes, and the auditory lesion may instead begin in hair cells or synapses, so benefit could reflect general cochlear antioxidant or anti-inflammatory activity rather than interception of the ACOX1 causal route (DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886; DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894). Ebselen also has broad selenium-thiol pharmacology, acting as a rapid thioredoxin oxidant that can inhibit protein-disulfide reduction (DOI:10.1073/pnas.122061399), and it promoted calcium release, uncoupling and swelling in isolated mitochondria (DOI:10.1179/135100000101535924), providing rival or adverse mechanisms. The critical unknowns are thiol availability, exposure at the relevant subcellular and tissue compartments, direct lowering of peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide and 4-HNE, and coupling of that target engagement to glial, axonal, hearing and lesion outcomes; adequate exposure without biochemical target engagement would refute the delivery premise, whereas biochemical engagement without tissue or functional rescue would weaken peroxide as a material driver.

name: Clemastine
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Human pathology establishes material spinal axon and myelin destruction, but viable axons, recruitable progenitors, and the therapeutic window for compensatory remyelination have not been demonstrated. Sources: DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Early remyelination could support surviving axons, but prolonged dosing can exhaust progenitors and provoke inflammatory or pyroptotic injury, making benefit strongly stage- and cell-state-dependent. Sources: DOI:10.1002/ana.27098; DOI:10.1172/jci183941
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug oligodendrocyte differentiation and myelination are strongly supported, including oligodendroglial M1-receptor dependence, although duration-dependent adverse lineage effects limit uniform causal interpretation. Sources: DOI:10.1093/brain/awx312; DOI:10.1002/ana.27098
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Oral dosing produced a CNS electrophysiological effect in adults, making biological reach plausible, but free spinal-cord exposure, pediatric exposure, and the concentration needed for structural remyelination remain unknown. Sources: DOI:10.1016/s0140-6736(17)32346-2; https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=cf8a3449-8bb3-4d5c-8d0d-557590e49ee5&version=2
empirical_translation_rationale: Clemastine preserved myelin and delayed axonal loss in rat spinal injury and improved a human visual-evoked-potential surrogate in multiple sclerosis, counterbalanced by harmful progressive-MS and prolonged-exposure findings. Sources: DOI:10.1007/s11064-021-03465-0; DOI:10.1016/s0140-6736(17)32346-2; DOI:10.1172/jci183941
hypothesis_report: Clemastine is a biologically coherent but highly conditional compensatory hypothesis for early Mitchell-syndrome spinal lesions: the active moiety, delivered in experiments and clinical use as clemastine fumarate, can drive oligodendrocyte-progenitor differentiation through antimuscarinic signaling, with oligodendroglial M1-receptor dependence demonstrated in hypoxic mouse white matter (DOI:10.1093/brain/awx312), and the supplied rat spinal-cord-injury study reports preserved myelin, delayed axonal loss, and functional improvement (DOI:10.1007/s11064-021-03465-0). Because Mitchell-syndrome cord pathology contains proportional myelin and axon destruction, gliosis, multitract extension, and later volume loss (DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894), the directional bridge is an inference that forcing differentiation only while viable long-tract axons and recruitable progenitors remain could restore axon-myelin support and slow secondary axonal attrition; it cannot replace destroyed axons or neurons, and it does not correct stabilized ACOX1 dimers, peroxide excess, or other upstream oxidative injury. Human translation is real but narrow: in the 50-person, single-centre ReBUILD crossover trial, 5.36 mg clemastine fumarate twice daily shortened visual-evoked-potential latency by 1.7 ms/eye and produced fatigue without serious adverse events (DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32346-2), but this was a short electrophysiological surrogate study in adult relapsing multiple sclerosis with preselected surviving optic-nerve axons, not evidence of spinal structural rescue, durable clinical benefit, or efficacy in ACOX1 disease. Important negative and null findings constrain the interpretation: in rabbit chronic demyelinating lesions, shorter exposure enhanced differentiation without increasing total oligodendrocyte density, whereas prolonged exposure exhausted the progenitor pool, induced senescence, and shifted macrophages/microglia toward a proinflammatory phenotype (DOI:10.1002/ana.27098); during developmental mouse myelination, more oligodendrocytes paradoxically accompanied fewer myelinated axons and nodes, thinner myelin, and slower conduction (DOI:10.3389/fcell.2022.841548), so oligodendrocyte counts alone would be a misleading efficacy readout. Most concerningly, a small open-label progressive-MS TRAP-MS arm stopped after 3 of 9 evaluable patients met prespecified safety criteria, with faster disability progression, increased CSF purinergic/pyroptosis signals, and ATP-dependent P2RX7-mediated pyroptosis in macrophages and human iPSC-derived oligodendrocytes (DOI:10.1172/JCI183941); advanced inflammatory MS is a rival biological context rather than a Mitchell-syndrome model, and the causal pyroptosis account lacks treated human CNS tissue, but macrophage-rich Mitchell lesions make this a material hazard rather than a dismissible artefact. A current US DailyMed label confirms marketed prescription clemastine fumarate for allergic rhinitis and uncomplicated urticaria/angioedema, not remyelination; it warns that safety and efficacy are unestablished below age 12 and that drowsiness is frequent (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=cf8a3449-8bb3-4d5c-8d0d-557590e49ee5&version=2), while the ReBUILD regimen exceeded the label's maximum daily fumarate dose and neither cord exposure at a remyelinating concentration nor exposure-response in children is known. No published or registered exact-disease use of clemastine in Mitchell syndrome was located in targeted searches. The decisive experiment therefore requires an early ACOX1-p.N237S neural system containing axons, oligodendrocyte lineage cells, and myeloid cells, with direct measures of myelin ultrastructure and conduction, axonal injury and survival, progenitor depletion/senescence, ROS, ATP-P2RX7-pyroptosis, and clinically achievable clemastine exposure, followed only then by longitudinal myelin-sensitive imaging, axonal biomarkers, lesion volume, and function in any human study.

name: hydralazine
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Disease models show a large 4-HNE-adduct signal alongside glial degeneration, but the signal is whole-animal and cell-specific carbonyl excess is not established in human Mitchell tissue. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Quenching reactive carbonyl propagation downstream of persistent peroxide is directionally coherent and falsifiable, but adduct remodeling, proteostasis, anti-inflammatory signaling, and vasodilation are rival routes. Sources: DOI:10.1002/cmdc.201500552; DOI:10.1124/mol.112.078956
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Direct comparative chemistry establishes hydralazine capture of 4-HNE and related carbonyls, although biological selectivity and the relative role of free-aldehyde trapping versus adduct-protein effects remain incomplete. Sources: DOI:10.1002/cmdc.201500552; DOI:10.1124/mol.112.078956
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Marketed systemic use establishes human dosing, but CNS carbonyl target engagement is unmeasured and hypotension, variable acetylation, and chronic lupus-like toxicity constrain escalation. Sources: DAILYMED:493a8b7e-5bb1-4db2-91a7-77ed87864131
empirical_translation_rationale: Systemic hydralazine lowered spinal acrolein adducts and improved motor and sensory outcomes in an inflammatory demyelination model, with concordance from a distinct carbonyl scavenger but small groups and mechanism mismatch. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41598-024-56035-z
hypothesis_report: Hydralazine is a plausible mechanistic probe of the reactive-carbonyl arm of Mitchell-syndrome injury: its hydrazine functionality directly captures 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4-HNE) and related reactive carbonyl species in comparative chemistry (DOI:10.1002/cmdc.201500552), while ACOX1 p.N237S produces excess peroxisomal oxidant flux, a dramatic rise in 4-HNE-modified proteins, and glial degeneration in overexpression models (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021). The directional inference is that lowering diffusible carbonyls and carbonyl-protein adduct propagation could improve glial survival downstream of the mutant enzyme even if ACOX1 dimerization, peroxide production, and the initiating lipid oxidation remain unchanged. Supporting empirical translation is limited but nontrivial: in an inflammatory mouse demyelination model, systemic hydralazine lowered spinal-cord acrolein adducts and was associated with improved motor and sensory outcomes, including when begun after symptom emergence, and a structurally distinct carbonyl scavenger produced a concordant benefit (DOI:10.1038/s41598-024-56035-z). This is not a Mitchell-syndrome model, however, and the small experimental groups, immune-pathology context, and possible anti-inflammatory or Nrf2-related effects prevent attribution of benefit solely to carbonyl trapping. Moreover, cell work indicates that hydralazine can preferentially attack carbonyl-adducted proteins and mobilize Hsp90, so cytoprotection may reflect adduct remodeling or proteostasis rather than simple interception of free aldehyde (DOI:10.1124/mol.112.078956). The disease-side 4-HNE signal was measured in whole-fly material rather than purified glia, patient CNS tissue has not established cell-specific 4-HNE excess, wild-type ACOX1 overexpression was itself toxic in Schwann cells, and no exact-disease use or testing of hydralazine was established. Hydralazine does satisfy the human-use qualification through a currently marketed prescription-tablet ANDA, but its intended vasodilator action creates hypotension and reflex-cardiovascular liability, exposure varies substantially with acetylator phenotype, chronic use carries a lupus-like syndrome warning, and the label does not establish CNS carbonyl target engagement (DAILYMED:493a8b7e-5bb1-4db2-91a7-77ed87864131). Thus, a reduction in 4-HNE/protein-adduct burden coupled to improved glial survival without normalization of upstream peroxide would support the proposed downstream-effector bridge, whereas a null result would remain ambiguous between carbonyl non-causality, insufficient CNS exposure, or competing injury mechanisms.

name: Edaravone
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Disease-specific p.N237S models establish oxidant production, 4-HNE-marked damage, and glial injury, although the exact downstream radical species and human cell-resolved relevance remain incomplete. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Intercepting downstream hydroxyl, superoxide, and peroxyl radical propagation while leaving ACOX1 and initiating peroxide unchanged is coherent, but dominant injury chemistry and reversibility remain assumptions. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.jss.2018.03.020; DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-compound chemical studies strongly establish scavenging of hydroxyl, superoxide, and peroxyl radicals, with relevant cellular protection but without direct clearance of the initiating hydrogen peroxide. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.jss.2018.03.020; DOI:10.1021/jp110400t
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Human systemic dosing is established, but animal brain exposure below 10% of plasma and high protein binding make relevant free spinal-white-matter exposure doubtful without target-site measurements. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.yebeh.2024.110159; FDA:NDA-215446-S000-LABEL
empirical_translation_rationale: Edaravone reduced peroxide-associated ROS and death in primary rat oligodendrocyte progenitors, but this acute exogenous-insult result has not translated to an ACOX1 model or human neural phenotype. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2018.01.018
hypothesis_report: Edaravone is a scientifically plausible downstream radical-interception hypothesis for Mitchell syndrome because the p.N237S ACOX1 lesion stabilizes an active oxidase dimer, increases glial hydrogen peroxide/reactive oxygen species and 4-HNE-marked lipid damage, and is associated with wrapping-glial and Schwann-cell death followed by axonal and myelin loss [DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021]. Edaravone scavenged hydroxyl, superoxide and peroxyl radicals in chemical systems [DOI:10.1016/j.jss.2018.03.020] and attenuated hydrogen-peroxide-associated ROS accumulation and death in primary rat oligodendrocyte precursor cells [DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2018.01.018], supporting the directional inference that it might interrupt secondary lipid-radical propagation and membrane injury in glia and axons even if mutant ACOX1 activity and the initiating peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide remain unchanged. That bridge is not demonstrated in an ACOX1-mutant system: the supportive glial experiment used acute exogenous hydrogen peroxide, did not distinguish direct radical trapping from broader stress signalling, and does not show direct hydrogen-peroxide clearance, while the disease evidence contains material artefacts and nulls, including toxicity from wild-type ACOX1 overexpression, whole-animal rather than cell-resolved 4-HNE measurement, unchanged early zebrafish oligodendrocyte counts and myelin transcripts, and incomplete antioxidant/inflammatory transcriptional responses [DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886]. Low CNS delivery is also a credible constraint: a blinded neonatal-rat study in a different structural-lesion disease found no acute antispasm effect and brain edaravone below 10% of plasma, so that negative result is not disease-mechanistic evidence against Mitchell syndrome but does challenge exposure in spinal white matter [DOI:10.1016/j.yebeh.2024.110159]; human target-site concentrations in spinal cord, peripheral nerve, Schwann cells and glia remain unknown, and 92% serum-protein binding further limits inference from total plasma exposure [FDA:NDA-215446-S000-LABEL]. The exact compound nevertheless satisfies a human-use qualification: FDA records show marketed approvals of intravenous Radicava and oral Radicava ORS for ALS [FDA:OOPD-478215], and a Phase I study found interpretable systemic pharmacokinetics with generally mild, reversible laboratory abnormalities and good tolerability in healthy adults [PMID:22762844], although the FDA label states that pediatric safety and effectiveness are not established and that its therapeutic mechanism in ALS is unknown [FDA:NDA-215446-S000-LABEL]. No published use or testing of edaravone in Mitchell syndrome was identified. The principal rival explanations are that hydrogen-peroxide signalling, peroxisome loss/integrated stress response, immune activity, or primary axonal injury rather than edaravone-reactive radical-chain propagation dominates the disease, and that established axon-myelin destruction is no longer reversible; accordingly, the hypothesis would gain specificity only if downstream lipid oxidation and glial/axonal injury fall despite persistent upstream ACOX1 and peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide, whereas verified target-site exposure without suppression of those downstream oxidation products would argue that edaravone's radical-scavenging action is insufficient.

name: Pioglitazone
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Myeloid accumulation is observed in human Mitchell white matter, but its state, timing, and causal materiality are unresolved and comparator peroxisomal-loss models point in opposing directions. Sources: DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894; DOI:10.3389/fnmol.2025.1542938
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Preserving phagocytosis while reducing inflammatory differentiation is coherent, but the CD68-positive cells may already be protective and the evidence transfers from peripheral monocytes in another demyelinating disease. Sources: DOI:10.1002/acn3.260; DOI:10.1186/s12974-019-1442-3
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Pioglitazone is an established PPARgamma agonist with exact-drug functional myeloid effects, but causal mediation and transfer to CNS microglia under p.N237S gain of function are incomplete. Sources: DOI:10.1002/acn3.260; DAILYMED:a3ae5cba-f495-4593-b8fc-5ada34790745
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Total plasma exposure makes reach conceivable, but greater than 99% protein binding and absent free brain concentration or CNS PPARgamma engagement leave relevant exposure materially unknown. Sources: DAILYMED:a3ae5cba-f495-4593-b8fc-5ada34790745
empirical_translation_rationale: At nominally achievable concentration, pioglitazone partially normalized inflammatory differentiation and restored myelin phagocytosis in human MS monocytes; a small MS trial adds only limited adjacent clinical support. Sources: DOI:10.1002/acn3.260; DOI:10.1016/j.jneuroim.2009.04.011
hypothesis_report: Pioglitazone is a marketed thiazolidinedione and PPARgamma agonist approved for glycaemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, so the candidate has established human use, but its proposed Mitchell-syndrome action is experimental (DAILYMED:a3ae5cba-f495-4593-b8fc-5ada34790745). The directional hypothesis is that increasing PPARgamma activity in the CD68-positive myeloid population of affected white matter could favour a regulated, clearance-competent state over a cytotoxic inflammatory state: 1 micromolar pioglitazone, chosen as a plasma-achievable concentration, partially normalized pro-inflammatory differentiation and restored defective myelin phagocytosis in ex-vivo peripheral monocytes from people with multiple sclerosis (DOI:10.1002/acn3.260). This action is relevant to the single Mitchell-syndrome autopsy in which increased microglia and perivascular macrophages co-localized with myelin and axonal injury (DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894), and to the disease-specific ACOX1 p.N237S oxidant-glial-injury axis (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021), but the bridge is inferential because the autopsy did not establish whether those cells caused injury or were performing protective debris clearance. Comparator findings pull in both directions: chronic microgliosis after myeloid-lineage Mfp2 loss did not produce neurological dysfunction (DOI:10.1186/s12974-019-1442-3), whereas conditioned medium from Acox1-null BV-2 cells injured neurons and oligodendrocytes, especially after LPS stimulation (DOI:10.3389/fnmol.2025.1542938); both are loss-of-function systems mechanistically different from p.N237S gain of function, and a p.N237S zebrafish model showed no increase in tested general inflammatory transcripts at its sampled stage (DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886). A small one-year randomized add-on study in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis established tolerability of 30 mg/day in 21 completers and reported less grey-matter atrophy, but no significant EDSS difference, making it a dosing-feasibility signal rather than efficacy evidence for Mitchell syndrome or this myeloid mechanism (DOI:10.1016/j.jneuroim.2009.04.011). The 1 micromolar cell result reflects nominal medium exposure and total plasma achievability rather than demonstrated free drug concentration or target engagement in human brain; pioglitazone is more than 99% serum-protein bound, and no retained source establishes its concentration in Mitchell-syndrome white matter (DAILYMED:a3ae5cba-f495-4593-b8fc-5ada34790745). No published use or trial of pioglitazone in genetically confirmed Mitchell syndrome was identified in targeted exact-disease and ACOX1 searches. A decisive test therefore requires a lineage-resolved p.N237S model with measured pioglitazone exposure and PPARgamma engagement, simultaneous phagocytosis and inflammatory-state readouts, and axon-myelin outcomes; it must also address the rival explanation that myeloid accumulation is downstream repair and the clinically material fluid-retention and heart-failure warnings, while recognizing that paediatric safety and effectiveness are unestablished (DAILYMED:a3ae5cba-f495-4593-b8fc-5ada34790745).

name: fasudil
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Human imaging establishes bilateral optic-pathway enhancement, but ROCK activation, junctional pathology, and whether leakage precedes rather than follows axon-myelin destruction are unknown. Sources: DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886; DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: ROCK-dependent barrier tightening is a coherent cited route to reduce active leakage, but it may alter enhancement without preserving neural tissue if leakage follows irreversible destruction. Sources: DOI:10.1186/s12987-022-00336-w; DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug ROCK inhibition produced functional barrier effects in primary-cell systems, but concentration-dependent adverse impedance effects and non-specific impedance components limit causal precision. Sources: DOI:10.1186/s12987-022-00336-w
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Parent and active metabolite have interpretable human pharmacokinetics and are measurable in CSF after subarachnoid hemorrhage, but clinical parent exposure is below the strongest barrier experiments and diseased-barrier CSF does not establish optic target-site reach. Sources: DOI:10.1007/s40263-024-01070-7; DOI:10.1016/j.jstrokecerebrovasdis.2004.10.006
empirical_translation_rationale: Fasudil improved impedance, TEER, permeability, and junctional readouts in an acute primary-rat BBB model, without disease-specific or human optic-pathway phenotypic evidence. Sources: DOI:10.1186/s12987-022-00336-w
hypothesis_report: Fasudil is a scientifically testable, imaging-level rescue hypothesis for the contrast-enhancing optic-pathway lesion, but it is not a correction of the ACOX1 gain-of-function lesion itself: by inhibiting Rho kinase it could relax actomyosin-dependent junctional tension, preserve claudin-5/occludin organization, and thereby reduce local tracer leakage and enhancement if ROCK-dependent neurovascular instability is an active and reversible component of the lesion. In a primary rat brain-endothelial/pericyte/astrocyte barrier model, fasudil increased impedance and TEER, decreased sodium-fluorescein permeability, increased claudin-5, and restored barrier readouts after oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation, providing the direct positive bridge (DOI:10.1186/s12987-022-00336-w); however, the model represented acute ischemic injury rather than ACOX1-mutant human optic tissue, the monoculture permeability decrease under injury was only a trend, 100 micromolar fasudil reduced impedance, and impedance itself combines cell number, adherence, morphology, and junctional tightness, so the result could partly reflect cytoprotection or altered cell shape rather than specific junctional repair. The most robust injured-barrier experiments used 10 micromolar fasudil whereas the same paper cited a clinical peak parent-drug concentration of about 0.36 micromolar, making exposure a material translational uncertainty even though an effect against a thromboxane-driven co-culture perturbation occurred at 1 micromolar. Disease relevance is anatomically plausible because the Mitchell-syndrome case had gadolinium enhancement across both prechiasmatic optic nerves, the chiasm, and both tracts, but the underlying ACOX1 N237S biology is stabilized active enzyme, excess peroxisomal reactive oxygen species, and glial injury, which fasudil does not directly normalize (DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886; DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021). Enhancement could instead be secondary leakage after irreversible axon-myelin destruction, necrosis, edema, or an immune lesion; AQP4/MOG testing was negative, the zebrafish model did not change the assayed general inflammatory or major myelin transcripts, and barrier tightening could improve an MRI marker without preserving vision or neural tissue (DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886). Human qualification is established but narrow: the current Japanese PMDA record lists marketed Eril injection for postoperative subarachnoid-hemorrhage vasospasm and ischemic symptoms, while warning about hypotension and intracranial bleeding (https://www.pmda.go.jp/PmdaSearch/iyakuDetail/100898_2190414A1033_1_07), and a randomized crossover phase-I study in 14 healthy adults reported no serious adverse events and interpretable oral/IV pharmacokinetics, although parent-fasudil exposure was low and variable and the active metabolite hydroxyfasudil had 69% oral bioavailability (DOI:10.1007/s40263-024-01070-7). Fasudil and hydroxyfasudil were measurable in CSF in patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage (DOI:10.1016/j.jstrokecerebrovasdis.2004.10.006), but those patients had acutely injured barriers and CSF drains, so this does not establish exposure at an intact or Mitchell-syndrome blood-optic-nerve barrier. No exact-disease use or testing of fasudil in Mitchell syndrome was identified, and the decisive unknowns are whether ROCK is activated in the enhancing optic lesion, whether leakage precedes rather than follows tissue destruction, whether clinically achievable unbound drug reaches the relevant optic-pathway neurovascular cells, and whether any barrier effect preserves axons, glia, or visual function rather than only suppressing contrast enhancement.

name: Probenecid
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Disease-specific p.N237S evidence supports an oxidant-glial-injury axis and human pathology establishes progressive peripheral axon and Schwann-cell damage, although abnormal glutathione export itself is not established. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Retaining glutathione is speculative because disease-cell efflux is unshown, MRP1 also exports oxidized glutathione, and transporter inhibition can worsen Schwann-cell viability under stress. Sources: DOI:10.1111/j.1471-4159.2006.03737.x; DOI:10.1248/bpb.b13-00046
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug evidence supports probenecid-sensitive glutathione transport and neuronal glutathione retention, but pannexin-1 and other organic-anion actions confound causal attribution to ABCC1. Sources: DOI:10.1054/bjoc.2000.1262; DOI:10.1152/ajpcell.00227.2008
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Human total plasma concentrations are measurable, but extensive albumin binding and lower tissue than plasma levels make the 100-micromolar culture action doubtful in unbound peripheral-nerve exposure. Sources: DOI:10.1002/jps.2600711114; DOI:10.2165/00003088-198106020-00004
empirical_translation_rationale: Probenecid preserved glutathione and reduced injury in mechanically stretched primary rat cortical neurons, a mismatched acute model that cannot establish the proposed peripheral-axon phenotype. Sources: DOI:10.1089/neu.2015.4342
hypothesis_report: Probenecid is a plausible but highly conditional redox-buffering hypothesis for Mitchell syndrome: ACOX1 p.N237S increases active ACOX1 and oxidant burden in glial models, antioxidant interventions suppress model phenotypes, and affected human peripheral nerve contains progressive axonal and Schwann-cell injury [DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894]. In a distinct mechanical-stretch model, 100 micromolar probenecid preserved intracellular glutathione and reduced injury in primary rat cortical neurons [DOI:10.1089/neu.2015.4342], while probenecid-sensitive glutathione export in MRP1-transfected cells supports the proposed transporter action [DOI:10.1054/bjoc.2000.1262]. The directional bridge is nevertheless an inference: retaining reduced glutathione in oxidant-stressed sensory neurons or Schwann cells could strengthen peroxide buffering, but neither an abnormal glutathione-efflux phenotype nor probenecid target engagement has been shown in ACOX1-mutant peripheral cells. MRP1 also exports oxidized glutathione during peroxide stress in astrocytes [DOI:10.1111/j.1471-4159.2006.03737.x], and MRP1 knockdown worsened viability in rat Schwann cells under a different stressor [DOI:10.1248/bpb.b13-00046], so transporter inhibition could impair protective detoxification and its net direction may depend on cell type and insult. Probenecid inhibits pannexin-1 channels in the same concentration range as transport processes [DOI:10.1152/ajpcell.00227.2008], making non-ABCC1 actions a material rival explanation for any protection. Healthy volunteers reached mean total plasma peaks of 35.3, 69.6, and 148.6 micrograms per millilitre after 0.5-, 1-, and 2-g oral doses [DOI:10.1002/jps.2600711114], but extensive albumin binding and generally lower animal tissue than plasma concentrations leave the free exposure attainable in human peripheral nerve at the 100-micromolar culture effect unresolved [PMID:7011657]. Probenecid has a current U.S. marketed prescription label for gout under an abbreviated new drug application, establishing human-use qualification while also documenting broad transporter-mediated interaction liabilities [DAILYMED:ab497fd8-00c3-4364-b003-b39d21fbdf38]; targeted searches found no prior probenecid use or testing in Mitchell syndrome or ACOX1 p.N237S disease. The critical unknowns are therefore cell-specific ABCC1 expression and reduced-versus-oxidized glutathione flux in the diseased axon-Schwann-cell unit, loss of any protective effect with selective transporter perturbation, separation from pannexin and other organic-anion-transporter actions, and pharmacologically attainable unbound nerve exposure.

name: Thioridazine
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: The stabilized, overactive p.N237S ACOX1 dimer and its linked peroxide and glial injury are directly established in disease-specific models and constitute a proximal actionable lesion. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Partial pathway braking could reduce ACOX1-coupled peroxide, but excessive peroxisomal inhibition demonstrably raises cerebral VLCFAs and the beneficial exposure window is undefined. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2012.08.086; DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Thioridazine inhibits peroxisomal beta-oxidation and ACOX1-dependent respiration, but direct human ACOX1 binding, mutant preference, potency, and separation from broad phenothiazine actions are absent. Sources: DOI:10.1016/0014-5793(85)81270-9; DOI:10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108421
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Human parent-plus-metabolite exposure approached micromolar levels, but relevant ACOX1 inhibition is undefined and dose-limiting QTc and neurologic toxicity sharply constrain sustained dosing. Sources: DOI:10.1182/bloodadvances.2018015677; DAILYMED:56b3f4c2-52af-4947-b225-6808ae9f26f5
empirical_translation_rationale: No ACOX1-disease phenotype is rescued; in an adjacent CNS model thioridazine reduced superoxide but did not prolong survival and only transiently improved motor performance. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2016.05.016
hypothesis_report: Thioridazine is a scientifically testable but pharmacologically hazardous pathway-brake hypothesis for Mitchell syndrome: ACOX1 p.N237S produces an overabundant active dimer with increased catalytic activity and glial oxidant burden, while thioridazine inhibits hepatic peroxisomal beta-oxidation in mice and suppresses ACOX1-dependent peroxisomal respiration in persister cells, supporting the directional inference that reducing excessive ACOX1 flux could lower its coupled hydrogen-peroxide output before irreversible axon-myelin loss (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.1016/0014-5793(85)81270-9; DOI:10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108421). The bridge remains indirect: no cited study demonstrates binding to human ACOX1, preference for p.N237S complexes, normalization of dimer persistence, or peroxisomal target engagement in human neural cells, and the parallel effects of ACOX1 knockdown and thioridazine do not exclude another phenothiazine action or a pathway-level artefact; consistent with such target ambiguity, CNS-exposed thioridazine lowered spinal-cord superoxide through NOX-inhibitory pharmacology in SOD1(G93A) mice but did not prolong survival and produced only transient motor improvement (DOI:10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2016.05.016). Excess inhibition is also directionally dangerous because thioridazine increased cerebral very-long-chain fatty acids and Aβ40 in rats, so benefit cannot be inferred from oxidant reduction alone (DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2012.08.086). Human exposure qualification is established but unfavorable for this use: a completed 13-person phase-I AML study obtained interpretable circulating exposure yet observed dose-limiting grade-3 QTc prolongation at 25 mg every six hours and neurological dose-limiting events at 100 mg every six hours, with the summed parent-and-metabolite DRD2-antagonist concentration approaching 10 μM at 50 mg every six hours (DOI:10.1182/bloodadvances.2018015677), and a current U.S. prescription label lists marketed NDC presentations under ANDA088004 but restricts the indication to refractory schizophrenia and warns of dose-related QTc prolongation, torsades, and sudden death (DAILYMED:56b3f4c2-52af-4947-b225-6808ae9f26f5). No exact-disease use or testing was found, and viability therefore depends on an as-yet-undefined exposure window that lowers ACOX1-dependent flux and peroxisomal peroxide while preserving lipid handling, with concurrent absence of a VLCFA rise and evidence of axon-myelin stabilization; unchanged dimer abundance would not itself falsify a catalytic-brake mechanism, whereas failure to separate ACOX1 engagement from NOX, dopamine-receptor, and other phenothiazine effects would leave the causal explanation unresolved.

name: Pexidartinib
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: A single human autopsy establishes CD68-positive microglial and perivascular-macrophage accumulation in injured white matter, but neither lineage, timing, nor a causal contribution to injury is established. Sources: DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Depleting the accumulated myeloid population has no secure beneficial direction because its role may be reparative, and near-complete PLX3397 depletion worsened injury and recovery in an adjacent spinal-injury model. Sources: DOI:10.1186/s12974-019-1442-3; DOI:10.1038/s41419-020-2733-4
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug studies strongly establish rapid depletion of adult-mouse brain microglia, although KIT, FLT3, peripheral-macrophage, and marrow effects prevent clean attribution to selective CNS CSF1R modulation. Sources: DOI:10.24272/j.issn.2095-8137.2022.389; DOI:10.3389/fimmu.2023.1283711
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Relevant normal-white-matter exposure is doubtful: macaque CSF concentrations were a very small fraction of plasma, and high-dose human glioblastoma exposure did not measurably reduce IBA1-positive cells at group level. Sources: DOI:10.1007/s00280-020-04071-7; DOI:10.1093/neuonc/nov245
empirical_translation_rationale: No drug-specific beneficial phenotype supports the complete hypothesis; adjacent studies instead report worsened spinal-injury outcomes after depletion and no group-level IBA1 reduction or tumor response in glioblastoma. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41419-020-2733-4; DOI:10.1093/neuonc/nov245
hypothesis_report: Pexidartinib could be used as a graded, time-limited CSF1R perturbation—not as an assumed treatment—in a lineage-resolved ACOX1 p.N237S white-matter model: the mutation stabilizes active ACOX1 dimers, raises glial oxidant burden and causes glial/axonal injury, while the single human autopsy found increased CD68-highlighted microglia and perivascular macrophages within injured white matter but did not establish their lineage, state, timing or causal role (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021; DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894). Inhibiting CSF1R-dependent survival should lower the accumulated population, so improved axon-myelin integrity would support harmful amplification whereas worsening injury would support debris-clearance or repair functions; both directions remain credible because peroxisomal-beta-oxidation-deficient microgliosis occurred without neurological dysfunction in Mfp2-deficient mice, Acox1-null microglial conditioned medium could damage neuronal and oligodendroglial cells, and near-complete PLX3397 depletion worsened tissue and functional outcomes after mouse spinal injury (DOI:10.1186/s12974-019-1442-3; DOI:10.3389/fnmol.2025.1542938; DOI:10.1038/s41419-020-2733-4). The action is empirically tractable—PLX3397 rapidly eliminates adult-mouse brain microglia (DOI:10.24272/j.issn.2095-8137.2022.389)—and the exact compound has interpretable human qualification because oral TURALIO is currently FDA-approved for adult symptomatic tenosynovial giant-cell tumor not amenable to surgery; however, it inhibits KIT and FLT3-ITD as well as CSF1R, carries a boxed warning for serious and potentially fatal liver injury with restricted REMS distribution, and lacks established pediatric safety or effectiveness (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/211810s013lbl.pdf). Translation to non-neoplastic white matter is uncertain: after a high single oral dose in macaques, CSF concentrations were only 0.04–0.51% of simultaneous plasma concentrations and drug was unquantifiable in half the animals (PMCID:PMC8459199), whereas 1,000 mg/day reached recurrent-glioblastoma tissue but produced neither a significant group-level reduction in IBA1-positive cells nor objective tumor responses, and an enhancing tumor does not establish exposure in intact white matter (DOI:10.1093/neuonc/nov245). Systemic PLX3397 also alters peripheral tissue macrophages and bone-marrow/circulating immune populations, including at doses that do not deplete microglia, so changes in lesions cannot be assigned to resident microglia without lineage-resolved pharmacodynamic measurements and complementary genetic or more selective controls (DOI:10.3389/fimmu.2023.1283711); CD68-positive perivascular macrophages, reversible depletion/repopulation dynamics, altered debris clearance, peripheral immunomodulation, and direct KIT/FLT3 effects are material rival explanations. No pexidartinib use or testing in Mitchell syndrome was identified, and the critical unknowns are normal-white-matter target engagement, a dose and schedule that modulate rather than indiscriminately eradicate CSF1R-dependent cells, whether p.N237S changes microglial CSF1R dependence or effector state, which CD68-positive lineage drives the lesion, disease-stage dependence, and whether any axon-myelin benefit can be separated from hepatotoxicity and pediatric risk.

name: Sodium phenylbutyrate
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: The proposed actionable deficit rests on one-time-point SKL reporter density in a transient zebrafish model without membrane-marker counts, ultrastructure, import testing, or pexophagic-flux measurement. Sources: DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Increasing peroxisome number is directionally insecure because the focal punctum decrease may be an artefact or adaptive turnover, and more organelles could amplify stabilized-ACOX1 flux and peroxide production. Sources: DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886; DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-compound experiments establish PEX11alpha-dependent, PPARalpha-independent peroxisome proliferation and orthogonal increases in PEX14- and SKL-positive organelles, though not in the relevant neural genotype. Sources: DOI:10.1128/mcb.22.23.8226-8240.2002; PMID:10716247
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Labeled human phenylbutyrate exposure is brief and below the sustained millimolar exposure used in the key proliferation experiment, with no Mitchell-relevant neural target-site exposure demonstrated. Sources: DAILYMED:d15f2cbf-4d22-40b5-8ef9-16b9d323a7f9; DOI:10.1128/mcb.22.23.8226-8240.2002
empirical_translation_rationale: Sodium 4-PBA increased peroxisome markers and improved selected functions in milder non-ACOX1 peroxisome-disorder fibroblasts and showed neural protection in unrelated inflammatory and cuprizone systems. Sources: PMID:10716247; DOI:10.1523/jneurosci.0312-22.2022
hypothesis_report: Sodium phenylbutyrate is a testable but explicitly conditional repurposing hypothesis for Mitchell syndrome: 4-PBA can drive PEX11alpha-dependent, PPARalpha-independent peroxisome proliferation, and loss of PEX11alpha abolished the response in mouse embryonic fibroblasts exposed to 5 mM for 10 days (PMID:12417726), while sodium 4-PBA approximately doubled orthogonally counted PEX14- and SKL-positive organelles in fibroblasts from patients with other peroxisome-biogenesis disorders and improved very-long-chain-fatty-acid beta-oxidation and plasmalogens only in milder cellular phenotypes (PMID:10716247). This action is directionally attractive only if the lower mCherry-SKL punctum density reported after transient ACOX1 N237S expression represents a persistent deficit of membrane-bounded, import-competent peroxisomes rather than altered reporter import or segmentation, accelerated adaptive pexophagy, or a transient quality-control phase; the focal study measured one time point, found no change in whole-larva pparab, pex11-family, or nbr1b transcripts, and did not measure membrane-marker counts, ultrastructure, biogenesis, fission, or pexophagic flux (DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886), while peroxisome-derived hydrogen peroxide is not universally sufficient to induce pexophagy (DOI:10.1089/ars.2017.6997) and auditory-hair-cell pexophagy can precede protective rebound proliferation (DOI:10.1073/pnas.1821844116). Neural translation is suggestive rather than disease-specific: 100 micromolar 4-PBA preserved peroxisomal markers in cytokine-stressed human microglia, and 4-PBA preserved myelin and neurofilament signals in a cuprizone mouse model (DOI:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0312-22.2022), but these effects do not establish PEX11-mediated rescue in ACOX1-mutant glia or hair cells and could include chemical-chaperone, transcriptional, or anti-inflammatory actions. The central counter-hypothesis is especially material because N237S stabilizes active ACOX1 and increases peroxide-linked glial injury (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021): increasing peroxisome number and beta-oxidation capacity could amplify rather than relieve oxidant production unless added organelles are functionally balanced. Human dosing qualification is established independently of this indication: a current New Drug Application label markets oral sodium phenylbutyrate for chronic urea-cycle disorders in adults and children, but after a 3-g fasted dose the mean phenylbutyrate Cmax was 146-169 micrograms/mL and its half-life only 0.5-0.8 hour, so sustained Mitchell-relevant neural exposure comparable with proliferation experiments has not been shown; phenylacetate neurotoxicity, potassium loss, and sodium burden also require attention in a disorder already characterized by hearing loss and neuropathy (DAILYMED:d15f2cbf-4d22-40b5-8ef9-16b9d323a7f9). No exact-disease use, trial, patient-derived-cell study, or stable N237S-model treatment was identified, so the decisive experiment is a concentration- and time-resolved study in patient-derived neural/glial cells and an endogenous-dosage N237S model that jointly measures PEX14 or PMP70 membrane counts, SKL import, ultrastructure and turnover, ACOX1 abundance and activity, peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide, lipid flux, and cell injury, with advancement only if durable functional-organelle restoration occurs without increased oxidant burden or toxicity.

name: Ricolinostat (ACY-1215)
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Human tissue establishes axonal swellings but provides no APP, organelle, ultrastructural, continuity, or kinetic evidence that defective transport is the actionable state. Sources: DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: HDAC6 inhibition can restore axonal cargo transport in adjacent systems, but Mitchell swellings have not been shown to contain reversible transport stalls or continuous axons. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41419-019-1920-7; DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug studies establish preferential HDAC6 inhibition, tubulin acetylation, and transport effects, but tubulin acetylation can be non-diagnostic and higher phenotypic concentrations recruit class-I HDAC activity. Sources: DOI:10.1097/j.pain.0000000000000893; DOI:10.3390/cancers12123734
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Published evidence describes ricolinostat as not brain penetrant, and no cerebral-white-matter exposure or target engagement is established despite systemic human dosing. Sources: DOI:10.7150/thno.67410; DOI:10.1016/s1470-2045(16)30375-8
empirical_translation_rationale: Ricolinostat improved transport-associated phenotypes in gp120-exposed cortical neurons and peripheral-nerve experiments, but no disease-specific or human neural benefit is available. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41419-019-1920-7; DOI:10.1097/j.pain.0000000000000893
hypothesis_report: Ricolinostat (ACY-1215) is an orally administered, preferential but not HDAC6-exclusive catalytic inhibitor whose proposed relevance to Mitchell syndrome is conditional: by preventing HDAC6-mediated α-tubulin deacetylation, it could increase microtubule motor engagement and cargo movement in axons, so a transport-stalled, still-continuous subset of the neurofilament-positive swellings in affected cingulate white matter might clear rather than progress to disconnection. The positive bridge is indirect but coherent: in gp120-exposed primary cortical neurons ACY-1215 prevented tubulin deacetylation and HDAC6 inhibition restored BDNF transport velocity, while peripheral-nerve experiments linked HDAC6 inhibition to increased α-tubulin acetylation and mitochondrial transport and confirmed a pharmacological effect with ricolinostat ([DOI:10.1038/s41419-019-1920-7]; [DOI:10.1097/j.pain.0000000000000893]); oral human dosing has also crossed a Phase-I-equivalent threshold, with no dose-limiting toxicities in a 21-patient phase Ib/II lymphoma study ([DOI:10.1002/onco.13673]) and clinically relevant exposure producing HDAC6-selective pharmacodynamic effects with a low level of class-I HDAC inhibition in a phase 1b combination study ([DOI:10.1016/S1470-2045(16)30375-8]). No current approved or marketed ricolinostat label was identified in FDA or DailyMed records, and no prior use or testing in Mitchell syndrome or ACOX1 gain-of-function disease was found. The central evidential weakness is that the human Mitchell lesion was a single terminal post-mortem observation without APP, organelle, ultrastructural, continuity, or transport-kinetic measurements, so its swellings may instead represent neurofilament compaction, demyelination-associated injury, glial oxidative failure, inflammatory reaction, or irreversible axon degeneration ([DOI:10.17879/freeneuropathology-2025-8894]); moreover, ricolinostat was reported not to be brain penetrant and rescued peripheral but not cognitive abnormalities in a cisplatin model, leaving exposure and target engagement in cerebral white matter unestablished ([DOI:10.7150/thno.67410]). Increased acetylated α-tubulin is itself not proof of functional rescue: in an unrelated cellular system ricolinostat produced sustained tubulin acetylation without robust inhibition of HDAC6 protein function, and phenotypic effects required higher, non-selective concentrations, highlighting both a target-engagement artefact and class-I/off-target rival explanation ([DOI:10.3390/cancers12123734]). The hypothesis therefore depends on demonstrating abnormal baseline axonal cargo kinetics, achievable local exposure with tubulin target engagement, and reversible swelling/continuity changes in a disease-relevant system; normal transport kinetics or persistent swellings despite target engagement would directly falsify the proposed directional bridge.

name: Chloroquine
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Excess pexophagy is unestablished; the focal evidence is a single SKL-punctum measurement that cannot distinguish organelle loss from import, segmentation, biogenesis, fission, or adaptive turnover. Sources: DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Blocking broad late autophagy could retain damaged peroxide-producing peroxisomes, and non-ACOX1 patient-cell systems show worsened peroxisomal metabolism and matrix import rather than functional rescue. Sources: DOI:10.3389/fcell.2021.661298; DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Chloroquine reliably inhibits late autophagic flux, mainly at autophagosome-lysosome fusion, but it is not pexophagy-selective and has substantial endolysosomal and Golgi polypharmacology. Sources: DOI:10.1080/15548627.2018.1474314
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Systemic human use and animal CNS tissue deposition make reach conceivable, but no tolerable human neural or cochlear pexophagy engagement is established and overlapping retinal, cardiac, neuromuscular, and auditory toxicity constrains dosing. Sources: DAILYMED:0a342f72-45f9-3e12-e063-6394a90ae33e
empirical_translation_rationale: Chloroquine increased a peroxisome marker without restoring function in one depletion model and failed or worsened function across patient-derived PEX1 systems. Sources: DOI:10.3390/ijms22157989; DOI:10.3389/fcell.2021.661298
hypothesis_report: Chloroquine is a currently marketed oral prescription antimalarial and amebicide whose relevant experimental action is broad inhibition of late autophagic flux, mainly by impairing autophagosome-lysosome fusion rather than selectively inhibiting pexophagy (DAILYMED:0a342f72-45f9-3e12-e063-6394a90ae33e; DOI:10.1080/15548627.2018.1474314). The Mitchell-syndrome hypothesis is therefore conditional: if ACOX1 p.N237S causes a sustained, injurious increase in pexophagic flux, slowing lysosomal disposal could raise the functional peroxisome complement and preserve lipid-metabolic and redox capacity, but the direction cannot be inferred from the present disease evidence because the sole focal finding is lower mCherry-SKL-positive puncta density at one time point in transiently overexpressing zebrafish neuromast hair cells, with no direct flux measurement and no significant whole-larva change in pparab, pex11a/b/g, or nbr1b (DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886). Cross-model evidence makes the bridge biologically testable but also exposes its main weakness: chloroquine partly restored ABCD3-positive peroxisome abundance in PEX16-depleted RPE-1 cells, yet cholesterol and plasmalogens did not recover (DOI:10.3390/ijms22157989), while chloroquine and other autophagy inhibitors produced no improvement and instead worsened peroxisomal metabolism and matrix-protein import across PEX1-G843D cell systems that included primary patient fibroblasts (DOI:10.3389/fcell.2021.661298). Thus, an increased puncta count could be a nonfunctional accumulation rather than rescue, and rival explanations remain reduced biogenesis or fission, altered SKL matrix import or image segmentation, and a transient adaptive quality-control phase; indeed, excess peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide was insufficient to trigger selective peroxisome degradation in another human-cell system, and auditory-hair-cell pexophagy can precede protective rebound proliferation (DOI:10.1089/ars.2017.6997; DOI:10.1073/pnas.1821844116). The label reports substantial tissue deposition and animal brain and spinal-cord concentrations above plasma, but disease-relevant human neural, glial, or cochlear target engagement at tolerable exposure is unestablished; this matters because nonselective autophagy blockade could retain oxidatively damaged, hydrogen-peroxide-producing peroxisomes, and the marketed label documents cardiomyopathy and arrhythmias, irreversible retinal injury, neuromyopathy, and auditory precautions that overlap important Mitchell-syndrome vulnerabilities (DAILYMED:0a342f72-45f9-3e12-e063-6394a90ae33e). Targeted literature and trial searches identified no exact-disease chloroquine use or testing, so the critical unknowns are whether pexophagic flux is actually elevated in endogenous-dose patient-relevant cells and whether chloroquine can lower that flux while increasing orthogonally measured membrane-bounded peroxisomes, matrix import, lipid metabolism, and redox control without increasing damaged-organelle burden or cellular injury.

name: trazodone
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: The premise rests on whole-larva atf4 transcript elevation without phospho-eIF2alpha, ATF4 protein, suppressed translation, cell identity, or concordant CHOP and slc7a11 changes. Sources: DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Lowering ATF4 output or restoring translation could remove a protective adaptation, and trazodone failed to rescue a distinct genetic neurodegeneration despite brain exposure. Sources: DOI:10.1093/pnasnexus/pgae429; DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0317404
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Trazodone can reduce ATF4 output and partially restore translation downstream of eIF2alpha phosphorylation, but its direct molecular target is undefined and the effect is not robust across stress contexts. Sources: DOI:10.1093/brain/awx074; DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0317404
exposure_feasibility_rationale: The original cell effect used 20 micromolar trazodone, well above the approximately 4 micromolar peak total plasma concentration in a human study, with no free-brain ISR engagement demonstrated. Sources: DOI:10.1093/brain/awx074; DOI:10.3389/fphar.2015.00224
empirical_translation_rationale: Drug-specific effects occur in unrelated stressed cells and prion or tauopathy mice, but a mechanistically adjacent SIL1-deficient model showed no neurodegenerative rescue. Sources: DOI:10.1093/brain/awx074; DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0317404
hypothesis_report: Trazodone is a conditionally plausible mechanistic probe, not a disease-supported treatment: in stressed mammalian cells and prion- and tauopathy-model mouse brains it lowered ATF4 output and partially restored translation despite persistent eIF2α phosphorylation, consistent with action downstream of eIF2α-P at the ternary-complex step, although its direct molecular target remains undefined (DOI:10.1093/brain/awx074). The Mitchell-syndrome bridge is weak and directional only if the reported whole-larva zebrafish atf4-transcript rise represents persistent eIF2α-P-driven translational repression; that model did not measure phospho-eIF2α, ATF4 protein, nascent translation, or cell identity, and ddit3/CHOP and slc7a11 were unchanged, while a distinct PEX5-import-stress system found ATF4 protective, so lowering ATF4 or restoring translation could remove an adaptation or merely alter an epiphenomenal partial signal rather than rescue ACOX1 injury (DOI:10.3389/fped.2024.1326886; DOI:10.1093/pnasnexus/pgae429). Translation across disease contexts is inconsistent: in SIL1-deficient woozy mice with PERK activation, trazodone did not reduce Purkinje-cell CHOP, prevent neurodegeneration, or rescue the principal motor deficits despite brain exposure, providing a material mechanistic null and leaving serotonergic effects as a rival explanation for a small behavioral change (DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0317404). The original cell work used 20 µM trazodone, whereas one healthy-volunteer pharmacokinetic study reported peak total plasma concentrations near 1.5 µg/mL (approximately 4 µM) and no serious adverse events, so free CNS exposure sufficient for ISR modulation and human target engagement remain unproven (DOI:10.1093/brain/awx074; DOI:10.3389/fphar.2015.00224). A current DailyMed label establishes approved adult use for major depressive disorder and thus substantial prior human exposure, but not pediatric, Mitchell-syndrome, or ISR efficacy (DAILYMED:1fd0fc6d-5b1c-9f6a-e063-6394a90a3b7c); no exact-disease use or testing was identified. The hypothesis therefore remains experimental and depends on disease-relevant cells showing the coupled state of elevated phospho-eIF2α and ATF4 protein with depressed translation, followed by translation restoration without loss of viability or peroxisomal function; absence of that coupled state, failure of translation rescue, or evidence that ATF4 is protective would favor noncanonical stress signaling and refute the proposed directional bridge.

name: Riluzole
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: A correctable BK deficit is inferred from a mechanistically different Pex5-loss mouse; Mitchell hearing loss has not been localized among hair cells, synapses, auditory nerve, glia, or central pathways. Sources: DOI:10.1002/advs.202300402; DOI:10.1186/s12920-023-01577-w
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: The net electrophysiological direction is insecure because riluzole activates BK only at higher concentration while inhibiting sodium current at lower concentration and can abolish auditory-nerve activity. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.lfs.2007.10.015; DOI:10.1097/00001756-200507130-00011
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact riluzole activates BK channels in inside-out human muscle patches, but the 10-micromolar action lacks native hair-cell context and competes with stronger sodium-channel pharmacology. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.lfs.2007.10.015; DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-52539-4
exposure_feasibility_rationale: The 10-micromolar BK effect is incompatible with the much lower clinically relevant concentrations and 96% protein binding absent evidence of unbound cochlear accumulation. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.lfs.2007.10.015; DAILYMED:ccead445-970c-46a1-9532-2848cc2aa3b6
empirical_translation_rationale: High-concentration intracochlear riluzole reduced acoustic-trauma threshold shift and dendritic injury, but cumulative exposure abolished nerve activity and the likely route differed from BK restoration. Sources: DOI:10.1097/00001756-200507130-00011
hypothesis_report: Riluzole provides a conditional way to test whether residual cochlear hair-cell BK conductance is limiting in Mitchell-syndrome hearing loss: 10 µM riluzole increased BK-channel activity from the cytosolic face of inside-out patches in differentiated human skeletal-muscle cells, while also inhibiting voltage-gated sodium current with an IC50 of 2.3 µM (DOI:10.1016/j.lfs.2007.10.015), and two BK activators transiently restored auditory-brainstem responses in Pex5-deficient mice whose cochlear BK expression was reduced (DOI:10.1002/advs.202300402). The directional inference is that opening channels that remain in ACOX1 p.N237S hair cells could accelerate repolarization and improve auditory output, but the premise is not yet demonstrated: Pex5 deletion is a peroxisome-import loss-of-function state in which oxidative-damage and mTORC1 readouts were null, whereas Mitchell syndrome is an ACOX1 gain-of-function redox disorder with established extra-auditory glial injury (DOI:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.02.021), and the increased auditory-brainstem-response latency in one patient is also compatible with auditory-neural or glial conduction disease rather than a primary hair-cell BK lesion (DOI:10.1186/s12920-023-01577-w). Riluzole has shown cochlear biological activity in a different setting, because 100 µM intracochlear exposure reduced threshold shift and dendritic injury after acoustic trauma, yet cumulative perfusion abolished auditory-nerve activity and the drug did not block glutamate-induced dendritic swelling, implicating suppression of presynaptic glutamate release rather than BK-mediated restoration as a rival explanation (DOI:10.1097/00001756-200507130-00011). The original BK observation may therefore be preparation- and concentration-dependent: an inside-out skeletal-muscle patch omits intact hair-cell accessory-subunit context and tissue exposure, clinically relevant riluzole concentrations around 1–2 µM preferentially stabilize inactivated voltage-gated sodium channels (DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-52539-4), and the marketed oral product is 96% protein-bound, so attainment of 10 µM unbound riluzole in cochlea is not established (DAILYMED:ccead445-970c-46a1-9532-2848cc2aa3b6). Riluzole is an approved and currently marketed U.S. prescription drug for ALS, satisfying the human-use qualification, although pediatric safety and effectiveness are unestablished (DAILYMED:ccead445-970c-46a1-9532-2848cc2aa3b6); no published report or registered trial of riluzole in Mitchell syndrome or ACOX1 p.N237S disease was identified. The critical unknowns are whether native ACOX1 p.N237S auditory cells actually retain a correctable BK deficit, whether riluzole opens their BK complexes at attainable unbound cochlear exposure, and whether the net effect preserves hair-cell and auditory-nerve signaling rather than suppressing it.
